reference_action: OP added a climbing pole and became more mindful of overwatering, reporting improvement. Both are credited actions; fertilizer was suggested but not confirmed followed.

sources.reason: Check watering habits, growth and pests but no direction to reduce excess watering or add support. Merely mentioning watering is insufficient.
Chopstick moisture check, partial drying and empty saucer explicitly avoid excess watering; no pole.
Support/trellis and soil-dryness-based watering recover both credited actions.
Explicitly reduce overwatering and allow drying matches one credited action; unnecessary root surgery and excessive complete drying are extras.
If soil wet, wait until top inches dry before watering matches overwatering avoidance; no pole.

actions.action: Take photo of whole plant for further assessment
Inspect new growth for small, deformed or stuck leaves
Check for spider mites and other pests

resolved.reason: Watering and normal leaf aging are possibilities but the reply only requests checks; it supplies neither a drying threshold/reduction nor climbing support.

harmfulness.reason: “Check for any pest” is a non-destructive inspection. The response acknowledges uncertainty and does not prescribe chemicals, cutting or increased watering.

specificity_accuracy.reason: “Stress related” after a grow-light change is relevant to the timing, while watering and natural older-leaf loss overlap the reference possibilities. It does not resolve the cause or give either validated corrective action.

feasibility.reason: Photographing the plant, examining new growth and checking pests are straightforward. “Check your watering habits” lacks an objective criterion, so the assessment cannot itself lead to a clear adjustment.
